title: Chapter 86 — The Delivered Base: Repeat Business & The Replacement Cycle
intro: Replacement-cycle timing, base mining, and lifetime-value arithmetic.

sections.title: The Replacement Cycle
sections.content:
Appliances have predictable lifespans. Refrigerators: 12-15 years. Dishwashers: 10-12 years. Ranges: 15-20 years. Washers and dryers: 10-12 years. Vent hoods: 15-20 years. Water heaters: 8-12 years.

Every customer in your delivered base will need new appliances on a predictable schedule. If you sold a family a fridge in 2020, they will need a dishwasher around 2025 and a washer/dryer around 2027. That is three more sales from one relationship — if you maintain it.

The rep who tracks replacement cycles in their CRM does not wait for customers to call when something breaks. They call proactively: 'Hi [name], it has been about 10 years since we set up your dishwasher. Is it still running well? Most dishwashers start showing their age around this time. If you are thinking about upgrading, the technology has changed a lot — I would love to show you what is available.'

sections.title: Base Mining
sections.content:
Your delivered base is your most valuable asset. These customers already trust you, already know your store, and already had a positive experience. Selling to them costs almost nothing compared to acquiring a new customer.

The proactive touch: 'Hi [name], it has been a year since we set up your kitchen. How is everything running? If you are thinking about any other upgrades, I am here whenever you are ready.' That call takes 90 seconds and it keeps you top of mind for the next purchase.

Base mining is not just about the next appliance. It is about the referral. Every satisfied customer knows 5-10 people who will need appliances in the next year. The annual check-in is your referral ask: 'If you know anyone shopping for appliances, I would love the chance to help them.'

sections.title: Lifetime Value Math
sections.content:
A single customer who buys from you at 35 will need approximately $15,000-25,000 in appliances over their lifetime — kitchen package, laundry, replacements as products age out, a second home or a renovation, and outdoor living.

Plus their referrals — conservatively 5-10 people, each worth $3,000-8,000 in first-purchase revenue. Some of those referrals become repeat customers who generate their own referrals.

One well-maintained customer relationship is worth $30,000-80,000 in lifetime revenue. That is why the 48-hour follow-up call, the annual check-in, the water filter reminder, and the referral ask matter so much. You are not being nice. You are investing in a compounding asset that grows every year you maintain it.

The rep who builds and maintains a delivered base of 500 customers has a $15-40 million revenue pipeline that will produce for the rest of their career. That is not a sales job. That is a business.
